html:
The Winyah were an Indigenous people of the South Carolina Lowcountry, around Winyah Bay, the Black River and the lower Pee Dee River, near today's Georgetown. Their language is not recorded, but they are usually grouped with the Siouan-speaking peoples of the Carolina coast.

A Spanish colony led by Lucas Vázquez de Ayllón may have landed near Winyah Bay in 1526, and failed within months. English traders from Charles Town reached the Winyah in the late 1600s. After the Yamasee War of 1715 to 1717 the small coastal peoples declined fast, and the Winyah merged with neighbours such as the Waccamaw, Pee Dee and Catawba.
